prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor kitchen corner with no people present as the camera wearer turns left from an upper cabinet (frame 1) toward a refrigerator (frames 2–4) and looks down at the floor corner (frame 5). In frame 1, the upper cabinet on the right is bright and within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m), occluded at the bottom edge by the frame boundary and situated above a dimmer counter (~1.0 m) and to the right of a glass-paned door (~1.2–1.5 m) whose upper panes open onto a dark, distant room (>2.5 m behind the door). Across frames 2 to 4, as the wearer rotates left and steps forward, the wooden cabinet side and adjacent refrigerator shift from the left into the foreground (~1.2 m down to ~0.5 m, entering arm's reach), creating a sharp vertical depth boundary that partially occludes a pitch-black open doorway on the left leading to a room 3–5 m behind the fridge, while a small floor bag is visible at the bottom of frame 2 (~1.0 m below the wearer). In frame 5, the upper-left corner where the refrigerator meets the wooden panel is extremely bright and close (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach), positioned above a distinct medium-bright curved pet bed on the floor at the bottom right (~0.8 m) and a darker floor strip on the bottom left (~1.2 m). This map makes the 3D planar geometry and the sharp foreground-to-hallway distance jump much clearer than the motion-blurred RGB frames, though it is unreliable on glass and dark surfaces—flattening the glass over the cabinet books in frame 1, failing to see through the glass door panes in frames 2–3, and distorting the flat black refrigerator surface in frame 5 into a bright upper bulge and dark lower recess.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies discrete objects across the camera wearer's leftward turn and approach in a person-free kitchen, starting in frame 1 by isolating twelve narrow vertical mask fragments labeled 'book' arranged in two rows inside the upper-right cabinet (~0.5 m away, within arm's reach), where the cabinet's horizontal wooden bar occludes the middle of the books. As the camera turns left in frame 2 and the books exit the right edge, the map fails to detect the actual black refrigerator entering on the far left (~1.5 m away) and instead mislabels the wooden side panel and the white glass-paned door (~1.0–1.5 m away in the center-right) as a single large 'refrigerator' mask. In frame 3, as the wearer faces the appliance at ~0.8–1.2 m, the mask shrinks to accurately bound the black side of the refrigerator in the center while misclassifying a white rectangular paper note attached to its surface (~0.8 m away, just entering arm's reach) as a 'tv'. By frame 4, the wearer is within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m) of the appliance, and the 'refrigerator' mask expands again to merge the black fridge face with the adjacent brown wooden cabinet panel on the right, before dropping all detections in frame 5 when the view tilts down toward the close-up fridge corner (~0.4 m) and floor cushion (~0.8 m). Compared to RGB alone, the map explicitly separates individual book spines in frame 1 and highlights the rectangular boundary of the note on the dark fridge in frame 3, but it is highly unreliable across views—confusing doors and wooden cabinetry with refrigerators, mislabeling paper as a television, and missing the floor bag, pet bed, doorway, and close-up surfaces in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, containing no yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the strip. Cross-referencing with the RGB images confirms that no other people are present in the kitchen or visible through the glass door on the right (~1.2–2.5 m away) or the open hallway doorway on the left (~3–5 m away), so there are no body orientations, gaze directions, or other-person reach zones in the scene. The absence of magenta hand detections also shows that as the camera wearer turns left from the upper book cabinet (~0.5 m away in frame 1) toward the refrigerator (~0.5–0.8 m away in frames 3–4) and looks down toward the floor cushion (~0.8 m away in frame 5), the wearer's own arms and hands remain occluded below or behind the camera's field of view despite the cabinet and refrigerator being within arm's reach. While the blank map reliably confirms the complete absence of visible bodies and hands even during heavy motion blur in frame 2, it provides no spatial layout, object boundary, or distance information on its own and requires the RGB or depth views to establish the surrounding scene geometry.
